name: opacity-swapy
title: Opacity Swapy Layout
description: Six pale tinted rows, each with a coloured line icon and a short benefit title, stacked in a narrow column. Dragging a row drops it to half opacity while the others slide apart to show where it will land.
use: A short list of items should be reordered by dragging the row itself with clear feedback.
avoid: Rows are a fixed 384 px wide and the order lives only in page state, so it resets on reload.
a11y: Rows drag only by pointer, with no keyboard route or focus handling, and nothing announces the new order. (keyboard: no, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A narrow centred column of six rounded rows in pale blue, pink, green, yellow, purple and cyan on black, each with a thin dashed outline, a small coloured icon at the left and a dark medium-weight label.
behaves: Dragging a row anywhere on its surface lifts it out of the stack at half opacity, and the rows above and below slide apart to open a gap. Releasing settles it into that gap, and the list holds the new order until the page reloads.
customise: No props: the six titles, icons and pastel classes sit in the items array in the file, and the 50 percent drag opacity and fixed width live in the source.
weight: light: Six static rows with a drag handler that only runs while a row is held.
demo: Benefit labels such as Streamline Operations, Decision Making, Reduce Costs and Future-Proof.
issues: The new order is only logged to the console and is lost on reload.
Slots reuse the item id, so slot and item keys collide.
The floating row covers two labels at once while it passes over the stack.
polishWhy: Soft pastel rows and clear drag feedback; the dashed outlines barely show and the page is bare.
